messages:
michelle_sales: Hey team — Zoomly trial is failing for the exec demo tomorrow. They see intermittent 401s and a bunch of 429s when hitting our hosted inference endpoint. Need urgent triage, customer is blocked :grimacing:

alex_sales_eng: Thanks Michelle. Can you paste the first 2 failing request IDs and timestamp? Also which model & region are they calling?

michelle_sales: Request IDs: req_3b9f1a and req_3b9f9c, seen ~2026-11-02T15:02:10Z. They're calling redwood-v1-large in us-east-1 (hosted). Demo uses short streaming responses (~200 tokens).

raj_engineer: On it. 401 + 429 combo usually means token rotation or a client hit the rate limiter fallback. Do we have full request headers + auth method?

michelle_sales: They use an API key passed in Authorization: Bearer <key>. Header sample from their support capture: ```Authorization: Bearer sk.zoomly.temp
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
X-Client-Id: zoomly-trial```

raj_engineer: That header looks fine. Can they reproduce with curl? Ask them to run this and paste the exact response including headers: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.zoomly.temp" -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-large","input":"hi"}'```

sarah_support: Also confirm whether they started multiple parallel streams from the demo client. 429s spike when many concurrent streams hit the same key. If it's for an exec demo, there might've been a stress test.

michelle_sales: Zoomly says they have 10 parallel tabs opened during the demo to simulate users. Demo user count usually 3. They did a smoke.

raj_engineer: 10 concurrent streaming connections is high for a trial key. Our hosted rate-limiter defaults to ~5 concurrent streams per key for free/trial. That explains the 429s. The 401s are interesting — might be intermittent because they've rotated a key and retried with an expired one.

michelle_sales: Customer asked if we can temporarily relax limits for tomorrow's demo. Is that possible?

oncall_lead: We can do a temporary quota bump. I'll need approval from Eng + Sales ops. Tagging @tanya_sec for any security gating. @deploy_bot can you show current quota for zoomly key?

deploy_bot: [bot] lookup-quotas zoomly-trial-key -> concurrent_streams=5, rps=20, burst=40

tanya_sec: We need an attestation: are they sending any PII in these requests? If so, we need to ensure logging is scrubbed and key scoping. Zoomly said it's anonymized demo data only. Please confirm in writing.

michelle_sales: Confirmed by customer: demo uses anonymized prompts, no PII. They signed our standard trial NDA.

raj_engineer: Two suggested immediate steps: 1) Temporary bump concurrent_streams to 20 for their trial key for a 4h window. 2) Ask them to switch to non-streaming (single response) for parallel tabs — streaming holds resources longer so costs spike. Which do we prefer for the demo?

alex_sales_eng: Sales prefers minimal friction. Let's do both: bump + advise non-streaming. But need price/committed throughput conversation for longer-term. michelle, can you confirm the ask is only for tomorrow 3pm–7pm UTC?

michelle_sales: Yes, demo window 2026-11-03 15:00–17:00 UTC. They asked for a safety margin, so +4h ok.

oncall_lead: I can apply the temporary quota. I'm going to open a short incident to track and rollback. Assigning to @sre_bot to monitor error rates.

sre_bot: [bot] incident created: INC-20261103-zoomly-poc. Monitoring enabled on endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Alert threshold: 429 rate > 10/min for 5m.

michelle_sales: Awesome. Also they asked about pricing — if they need sustained higher concurrency, what are the options and lead times?

alex_sales_eng: Short answer: we offer a Dedicated reserved slot or committed throughput add-on. Typical kickoff for dedicated is ~3–6 weeks (procurement + capacity). Committed throughput add-on can be applied within days and priced based on peak tokens/second. I'll follow up with a formal quote.

tanya_sec: For enterprise customers we'll need the security questionnaire filled. Zoomly asked about audit logs retention and KMS integration. Who owns the security response?

michelle_sales: I will own the questionnaire but need engineering answers on retention window and KMS options.

raj_engineer: Retention: request/response logs are retained 30 days by default on hosted, can be extended under an enterprise agreement. KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for Private deployments; hosted supports encrypted-at-rest with our KMS but not customer-managed unless Private. I'll add these to the questionnaire draft.

sarah_support: Back to the 401s — we should confirm they don't have simultaneous key rotation. Ask them to check token refresh logic. If they rotate keys mid-demo, requests with old token will 401 until updated.

michelle_sales: I'll ask Zoomly to freeze key rotation for the demo and run the curl test Raj requested.

raj_engineer: If they paste the full response we can confirm Retry-After header on 429. Example 429 response headers: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 15
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0```

michelle_sales: Zoomly pasted back a sample earlier, here's what they saw: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-RateLimit-Limit: 5
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Body: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded"}```

raj_engineer: Confirms concurrency limiter hitting. OK: I'll prepare the change request to bump concurrent_streams to 20 for key zoomly-trial-key between 2026-11-03T14:00Z and 2026-11-03T18:00Z. After that window we auto-revert back to 5.

oncall_lead: Change scheduled. Applying now.

deploy_bot: [bot] quota-update zoomly-trial-key -> concurrent_streams: 5 -> 20 (effective 2026-11-03T14:00Z, revert 2026-11-03T18:00Z). Change ID: CHG-9032

michelle_sales: Thanks! Zoomly will rerun the demo smoke at 14:30 UTC. Can someone from SRE stand by at 14:25?

oncall_lead: I'll be on standby. @sre_bot will post any 429 spikes to #incidents.

sre_bot: [bot] watch rule active for CHG-9032. Posting alerts to #incidents.

michelle_sales: One last customer ask — if they move to Dedicated, can we guarantee lower tail latency? They want <200ms p95 for short prompts.

raj_engineer: Dedicated with pinned GPU pools + autoscaling gives much tighter latency profiles. We can run a latency benchmark with their workload. For contractual SLAs we typically offer p95 targets based on committed capacity; I'll schedule a perf test once they commit.

michelle_sales: Perfect. I'll confirm the no-PII note and have their team run the curl test. Will report back here with results. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround :pray:

alex_sales_eng: I'll draft a follow-up email: 1) confirm temp quota bump + window, 2) recommended non-streaming fallback for parallel tabs, 3) pricing options and next steps for Dedicated/committed throughput, 4) ask to freeze key rotation + confirm anonymized data. Will send within 30m.

michelle_sales: Got it. Zoomly just posted the curl output (14:31Z): ```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"id":"resp_7f3","output":"hi there"}``` — demo smoke passed after bump, no 429s observed.

oncall_lead: Closing incident watch after 30m of stable metrics. Reverting quotas at the scheduled time.

michelle_sales: Closing on our side too. I'll attach the security notes and the positive test log to the questionnaire. Thanks all :tada:
